correctness.rationale: The claim is reconstructed directly from the published definitions. Under an arbitrary invertible linear map, the codimension-one and codimension-two Jacobian formulas show that every facet mass and every ridge conductance acquires the same factor \(|\det A|\). Hence the Rayleigh form is affine invariant. Reduction to an axis-aligned box gives common facet mass \(M=2^{n-1}\prod_k a_k\) and common inter-direction conductance \(C=2^{n-2}\prod_k a_k\). For even functions the numerator is \(4C\) times the complete-graph difference sum and the denominator is \(2M\) times the centered square sum; \(4C=2M\) and the exact identity \(\sum_{i<j}(x_i-x_j)^2=n\sum_i(x_i-\bar x)^2\) finishes the proof. Constants form the one-dimensional zero eigenspace and the remaining even space has dimension \(n-1\). The included exact-rational script checks representative dimensions but is not used as a proof of the all-dimensional statement.

value.rationale: Parallelotopes are not an arbitrary test family: the originating paper explicitly singles them out in the extremal multiplicity discussion. The exact identity calibrates the newly introduced discrete centro-affine operator on that canonical family, supplies equality at \(n\) for every even nonconstant mode, and determines the multiplicity \(n-1\) exactly. This gives a reusable benchmark for extremal and stability questions and clarifies that the multiplicity-refined lower bound is numerically saturated by the natural candidate family, without claiming a converse characterization or global minimality.
